first_impression.summary_in_own_words: A planning service, Wedded Concierge, that will match me with an advisor to plan a wedding somewhere in Portugal. Lots of legal detail up top. No price, no proof they have done one, just a form to fill in.

attention_map.quote: a legal wedding in Portugal for foreign couples starts at least one month ahead
attention_map.why: A real, checkable number in the first lines, not fluff. Good start. But 'Wedded Concierge plans weddings in Portugal' is a claim with nothing behind it yet.

attention_map.quote: Planned by Wedded Concierge, with one Wedded Advisor from enquiry to the wedding weekend.
attention_map.why: It sits where the proof should be and contains no proof. No number, no review, no named wedding. It just repeats the hero sentence.

attention_map.quote: roof works with scaffolding run to the first quarter of 2027
attention_map.why: Pretty, but tourist-guide stuff. I did notice they admit the Monserrate scaffolding, which is the kind of catch nobody else tells you. That earns a point.

Five cards, and every one says 'spring and autumn, as a national guide' and 'Guests: Ask your Wedded Advisor'. That is the same card five times. Nothing I can compare against the tabs I have open: no capacities, no venues, no prices.

attention_map.quote: state events can cancel bookings at Queluz or the National Palace of Sintra. Nothing may be fixed to the heritage.
attention_map.why: This is what I look for: the catch, stated plainly, with a link to the official rules. But it stops there. If the state cancels my date, what do you do for me? Silence.

attention_map.section: What Your Wedded Advisor Checks in Every Venue Contract
attention_map.quote: exclusive use can mean paying for rooms your guests do not fill
attention_map.why: Best part of the page for me. Rooms, buy-out, minimums, VAT: exactly where hidden costs hide. This is the first actual reason to use them over going direct.

attention_map.section: Plan step by step: Marrying legally and Entry rules
attention_map.quote: Witnesses are optional: two to four may take part.
attention_map.why: Detailed, sourced to government sites, dated 'Checked October 2026'. I checked the one month, six months, documents and witnesses against the hero and FAQ and they match. This is the most trustworthy part of the page.

attention_map.section: Plan step by step: registry and consular fees
attention_map.quote: The civil registry charges a fee for the ceremony.
attention_map.why: Everything else in this tab has a number and a source, then the fee just says 'a fee'. Same with 'a consular notarial fee applies'. A government fee is public; leaving it blank makes me wonder what else is being kept vague.

attention_map.quote: What a wedding in Portugal costs depends on five things: your guest count, the region, the season, how many nights you take the venue and whether you book it for exclusive use.
attention_map.why: A heading that says 'What a Wedding in Portugal Costs' and then not one figure. That is the line every planner uses to get you on a call. I came here to gauge prices and I still cannot.

attention_map.section: See What a Portugal Wedding Weekend Includes
attention_map.quote: There is no set Portugal package. ... it can include: ... An on-the-day coordinator
attention_map.why: Honest that there is no package, but 'can include' a coordinator means it might not. Is the coordinator extra? Who pays? This is the only hint at what happens on the day and it is a maybe.
A guest website sign-up in the middle of a wedding planning page. Feels like a side sell.

attention_map.section: Plan Your Portugal Wedding with One Wedded Advisor
attention_map.quote: Portugal properties are still being confirmed, so your Wedded Advisor tells you what applies to your dates.
attention_map.why: 'Wedded Privileges' with nothing confirmed. Reads like a perk that does not exist yet. Also nothing here says what the Concierge itself costs me. Is it free? A fee? A commission from venues? Not a word.

attention_map.quote: There is no single average: the cost depends on your guest count, the region, the season...
attention_map.why: Legal and beach answers are solid and consistent with the tabs. The cost answer is the same non-answer again, now twice on the page.

attention_map.quote: Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodriguez's wedding
attention_map.why: After a page of careful government sources, a row of celebrity wedding gossip, two of them about the same couple. Cheapens the whole thing.

questions_answered.question: What is NOT included in the from price?
questions_answered.evidence: There is no from price at all, and no list of inclusions or exclusions. Costs tab and FAQ 4 both say it 'depends'. The Concierge's own fee is never mentioned. Even the registry fee is 'a fee'.

questions_answered.question: Are these facts consistent across the page?
questions_answered.evidence: One month minimum, six months to marry, five regions, four airports, five Parques de Sintra venues, beach permit rule and Monserrate works ('first quarter of 2027' / 'early 2027') all line up between hero, tabs and FAQ. Only small wobble: a 'Milestone birthday' card but no Birthday option in the form.

questions_answered.question: What proof is there that this team has done this venue before?
questions_answered.evidence: No real weddings, no reviews, no numbers, no named venue they have worked with. The proof strip says only 'Planned by Wedded Concierge'.

questions_answered.question: Why book through you and not the venue directly?
questions_answered.evidence: 'your one contact at Wedded Concierge, instead of one conversation per venue' and checking 'each venue contract for rooms, buy-outs, minimums and VAT before you sign'. A real reason, but without knowing what the service costs I cannot weigh it.

questions_answered.question: What happens if something goes wrong on the day?
questions_answered.evidence: Only 'it can include: An on-the-day coordinator'. Nothing on a state event cancelling a palace booking, rain plan beyond 'plan a covered option', or who is responsible.

objections_triggered.objection: From price with no inclusions list means hidden costs
objections_triggered.triggered_by: No price anywhere, Costs tab with no figures, 'There is no set Portugal package', and no word on what the Concierge charges.
'Wedded Concierge plans weddings in Portugal' repeated three times (hero, proof strip, advisor section) with no real weddings, reviews or numbers.
'The civil registry charges a fee for the ceremony.' and 'a consular notarial fee applies.'
Not triggered: the legal timings and counts match throughout.

trust_signals_noticed: Government sources linked by name and 'Checked October 2026'
The venue contract checklist: rooms, buy-out, per day or per guest minimum, VAT
Admitting the catches: state events cancelling palace bookings, Monserrate scaffolding to 2027, beach permits
Honest 'There is no set Portugal package' instead of a fake package
Consistent numbers across hero, tabs and FAQ
No urgency tactics and almost no superlatives
turn_offs_noticed: A 'What a Wedding in Portugal Costs' heading with no costs
Five identical region cards ending in 'Ask your Wedded Advisor'
Celebrity gossip links (Ronaldo twice) at the bottom

emotional_response.overall: Grudging respect for the homework, frustration at the money silence
emotional_response.trust: Trust the legal information; do not yet trust the service
emotional_response.feeling_at_end: This is a well-researched lead form. Every road ends at 'ask your Wedded Advisor'.

payload.decision_reason: I have to decide this week and I compare like for like. This page gives me nothing to compare: no price, no inclusions, no idea what the Concierge charges, and no proof they have planned a single wedding in Portugal. The legal guide and the contract checklist are genuinely good, but they are free information, not a reason to hand over my details. The other tabs at least show a number.
payload.verbatim_reaction: OK, this is the most thorough page I've read on the legal side, and nothing contradicts itself, which is rare. But what's the catch? I read the whole thing and still don't know what a wedding here costs, what you charge, or whether you've ever actually done one. 'Costs depend on five things' isn't an answer, it's a sales call. And a celebrity gossip row at the end? I'll copy the marrying-legally bit into my notes and go back to the planners who put a number on the page.
